messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: ggplot2 blog
parts:
Hi all,

I'm thinking about setting up a ggplot2 blog (probably on tumblr) that
would collect links of interest about ggplot2 (and visualisation in
general) from around the web. I've tried to do blogs in the past, and
I'm pretty hopeless at it (I just don't have the time), I was
wondering if anyone would be interested in contributing on a regular
basis. I don't think it would be a huge amount of work - just whenever
you see something interesting related to ggplot2 you'd need to post on
the blog.

I'm hoping to get maybe two people who would aim to post something
once a week, and then maybe a few more occasional contributors.
Please let me know if you'd be interested in helping out.

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 blog
parts:
Hi,

I would be keen to give it a try, not sure how often though. Should
the posts be only links to other sources, or could they bring new
content to the web too? (e.g. the occasional tip, how-tos, general
discussion of graphics)

Cheers,

baptiste

messages.subject: RE: ggplot2 blog
parts:
Maybe an aggregator type set up like 
http://www.statsblogs.com/  or 
http://www.r-bloggers.com/  would be more appropriate.  That way one person isn't keeping it going the whole time, plus individuals could also put the blog on Rbloggers etc as well if you so desired and just have a ggplot category that dictates sending it to the ggplot blog.  Hope this makes sense as I just started getting into blogging a about 2 weeks ago (as I was inspired by Rbloggers).
Tyler

messages.author: e68a1208f312170f
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 blog
parts:
Hi Hadley --

That sounds fun. My slant is mostly bioinformatics related to nextgen DNA sequencing, but I plot all kinds of stuff and love to peruse visualization-related topics. I'd be happy to commit to at least a post per week for 3 months. I'm guessing I could continue after that. One thing that I'd like to post is examples of ggplot usage in publications.

s

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 blog
parts:
I’d suggest a couple of features. It would be great to choose software that allows easy addition of images, obviously, but also that can syntax highlight R code.

Short screencasts are a great way to spread information, so a way to embed video from a server than handle that would be excellent.

The ability to add pages would allow people to build faq items that point into the blog, and accumulate information at a level a bit more systematic than single blog posts like to be.

Other than that, I think this is a great idea! 

It lowers the entry cost and creates a small incentive for people to help others with ggplot2.

Best, t
